```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

`top_fit_custom()` supports scientifically defined subtype groupings that are
not represented by TOP's predefined hierarchical structures.

```{r data}
library(TOP)
data("data", package = "TOP")

y <- data[, 1:5]
snp <- data[, 6, drop = FALSE]
pc1 <- data[, 7, drop = FALSE]
z_standard <- GenerateZstandard(y, missingTumorIndicator = 888)
```

Rows of the custom design correspond to the retained first-stage subtypes.
Columns define custom second-stage effects. This example maps the cross-classified
subtypes into five groups based on hormone-receptor status, HER2, and grade.

```{r design}
design <- matrix(0, nrow(z_standard), 5)
colnames(design) <- c(
  "HR+_HER2-_lowgrade",
  "HR+_HER2+",
  "HR+_HER2-_highgrade",
  "HR-_HER2+",
  "HR-_HER2-"
)

hr_positive <- z_standard[, 1] == 1 | z_standard[, 2] == 1
her2_positive <- z_standard[, 3] == 1
high_grade <- z_standard[, 4] == 2

design[hr_positive & !her2_positive & !high_grade, 1] <- 1
design[hr_positive & her2_positive, 2] <- 1
design[hr_positive & !her2_positive & high_grade, 3] <- 1
design[!hr_positive & her2_positive, 4] <- 1
design[!hr_positive & !her2_positive, 5] <- 1

table(rowSums(design))
```

Every retained subtype must map to at least one custom effect. Overlapping
columns are allowed when scientifically intended, provided the resulting model
is identifiable.

```{r fit}
custom_fit <- top_fit_custom(
  y = y,
  covariate = snp,
  design = design,
  adjustment = pc1,
  missing_value = 888
)

custom_fit$second.stage.test
custom_fit$global.test
```

The fitted object uses the same `top_model` methods as `top_fit()`.

```{r methods}
custom_fit
head(coef(custom_fit))
```
